ryans.name: Ryan (@ryangrowthh)
ryans.title: Marketer; distribution for @milesdeutscher and @aiedge_
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan**, who posts on X as **@ryangrowthh**, is a marketer based in Seattle, Washington [1]. His X bio describes him as a "marketing guy who builds big brands" and says he is "building mass distribution" for @milesdeutscher and @aiedge_ [1]. His X account was created in May 2026 [1].
known_for: Using Grok Bot for X content, about 2M views in his first two weeks on X (his figure)

ryans.name: Ryan Anderson
ryans.title: Co-founder and CEO of Filevine
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Anderson** is an American entrepreneur and former litigator who co-founded **Filevine**, a Salt Lake City–area legal technology company, and serves as its CEO [1][2].

ryans.name: Ryan Blaney
ryans.title: NASCAR Cup Series driver for Team Penske
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Blaney** (born December 31, 1993) is an American stock car racing driver who drives the No. 12 Ford Mustang Dark Horse for Team Penske in the NASCAR Cup Series [1][2]. He won the NASCAR Cup Series championship in 2023 [2][5]. Team Penske lists his birthplace as Hartford, Ohio, and his residence as Mooresville, North Carolina [2].

ryans.name: Ryan Breslow
ryans.title: Co-founder and CEO of Bolt
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Breslow** is an American entrepreneur and co-founder of **Bolt**, a checkout and payments software company for online retailers. After stepping down as CEO in early 2022 amid controversy, he was reinstated as CEO in March 2025 [1][3].
known_for: Bolt's 2022 valuation peak and later crash

ryans.name: Ryan Carson
ryans.title: Founder of Treehouse; serial entrepreneur
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Carson** is a British-American entrepreneur known for co-founding the online coding school **Treehouse**, which he led until its December 2021 acquisition, and for earlier companies DropSend and Carsonified [1][2][3].

ryans.name: Ryan Castro
ryans.title: Reggaeton artist
ryans.lead_summary: **Bryan David Castro Sosa** (born 1994), known professionally as **Ryan Castro**, is a Colombian reggaeton and dancehall singer-songwriter. Nicknamed “El Cantante del Ghetto,” he went from busking on Medellín buses to international hits including “Mujeriego,” “Jordan,” and “Quema” with Peso Pluma [1][2][3].

ryans.name: Ryan Cohen
ryans.title: Chewy co-founder; GameStop chairman and CEO
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Cohen** is a Canadian-born entrepreneur and investor best known as co-founder of online pet retailer **Chewy** and as chairman and CEO of **GameStop** [1][5][6].
known_for: GameStop chairman and CEO; 2021 meme-stock era

ryans.name: Ryan Cohen
ryans.title: Chairman and CEO of GameStop; co-founder of Chewy
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Cohen** (born 1986, according to Wikipedia) is a Canadian businessman and investor. He co-founded the online pet retailer Chewy in 2011 and is chairman and chief executive of GameStop [1]. PetSmart bought Chewy in 2017 for $3.35 billion, which Fortune and Wikipedia describe as the largest e-commerce acquisition at the time [1][3].
known_for: $3.35 billion sale of Chewy to PetSmart
GameStop turnaround as chairman and CEO

ryans.name: Ryan Coogler
ryans.title: Filmmaker
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Kyle Coogler** (born May 23, 1986) is an American filmmaker. He directed *Fruitvale Station* (2013), *Creed* (2015), *Black Panther* (2018), *Black Panther: Wakanda Forever* (2022), and the original horror film *Sinners* (2025), and co-founded the production company Proximity Media [1][2].

ryans.name: Ryan Craig
ryans.title: Head coach of the Vegas Golden Knights
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Craig** (born January 6, 1982) is a Canadian ice hockey coach and former centre who is head coach of the Vegas Golden Knights of the NHL [1][3]. He was named the franchise's fifth head coach on June 17, 2026, replacing John Tortorella [1][2]. He was an assistant on the Vegas staff that won the Stanley Cup in 2023 [1].
known_for: Fifth head coach of the Vegas Golden Knights
2016 Calder Cup as Lake Erie captain

ryans.name: Ryan Cwynar
ryans.title: Software engineer; creator of All The Ryans
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Cwynar** is a software engineer and entrepreneur. He operates **Byldr Software LLC** and is the creator of **All The Ryans** (alltheryans.com), the encyclopedia this page belongs to [1][2][3].

ryans.name: Ryan Dahl
ryans.title: Creator of Node.js and Deno
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Dahl** (born 1981) is an American software engineer best known for creating **Node.js**, the JavaScript runtime that made server-side JavaScript practical at scale, and later **Deno**, a secure TypeScript-first runtime built with V8 and Rust [1][2][4].

ryans.name: Ryan Day
ryans.title: Head football coach at The Ohio State University
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Patrick Day** (born March 12, 1979) is an American college and professional football coach and former collegiate quarterback who serves as the head football coach at The Ohio State University [1][2][4]. Named to succeed Urban Meyer on December 4, 2018, after going 3–0 as acting head coach at the start of the 2018 season, Day officially took over as Ohio State's head coach on January 2, 2019 [1][2][3].
known_for: Head football coach at Ohio State University (2019–present)
Winning the 2024 College Football Playoff National Championship
2019 Big Ten Coach of the Year and five CFP appearances
Childhood and adolescent mental health advocacy with On Our Sleeves

ryans.name: Ryan Dunwoody
ryans.title: Hardware engineer; co-creator of pi-top; Powerhouse founder
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Dunwoody** (born 1990 or 1991) is a British hardware engineer and entrepreneur based in Shenzhen, China [3][6]. With Jesse Lozano he co-created **pi-top**, a Raspberry Pi laptop kit that Guinness World Records lists as the first 3D-printed laptop, dated 9 November 2014 [1]. He later founded the motor-control company Motormaster and, in 2025, **Powerhouse Engineering**, a Shenzhen company that offers hardware startups engineering, prototyping and manufacturing support [6][7].
known_for: Co-creating pi-top, Guinness World Records' first 3D-printed laptop

ryans.name: Ryan Fleury
ryans.title: Systems programmer; RAD Debugger developer
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Fleury** is an American software engineer who works on development tools in the games industry and writes at **Digital Grove** (dgtlgrove.com) [1][6][7]. He is a Senior Engine Programmer at Epic Games associated with RAD Game Tools and is the lead developer of the open-source **RAD Debugger** [6][7].

ryans.name: Ryan Florence
ryans.title: Web developer; co-founder of Remix and React Training
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Florence** is an American web developer and educator who created the first version of React Router in May 2014 [1]. With Michael Jackson, he co-founded React Training in 2015 [2][3]. He later co-founded Remix Software with Michael Jackson, with Kent C. Dodds also described as a co-founder in interviews [2][9].

ryans.name: Ryan Garcia
ryans.title: American professional boxer
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Garcia** (born 1998) is an American professional boxer from Victorville, California [6]. Nicknamed "King Ry," he has held the World Boxing Council (WBC) welterweight title since February 2026 [5][6][7]. He previously won the WBC interim lightweight title in 2021 [1][2].

ryans.name: Ryan Giggs
ryans.title: Welsh former footballer and manager
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Joseph Giggs** (born 29 November 1973) is a Welsh former professional footballer and coach [1][2]. He spent his entire club playing career at Manchester United (1990–2014), making 963 appearances and winning 13 Premier League titles and two UEFA Champions League titles [2][3]. He later managed the Wales national team from 2018 until resigning in June 2022 [4][5].

ryans.name: Ryan Gosling
ryans.title: Actor and musician
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Thomas Gosling** (born November 12, 1980) is a Canadian actor and musician. He moved from child television to acclaimed independent films and major studio hits, earning Academy Award nominations for *Half Nelson*, *La La Land*, and *Barbie* [1][2][3].

ryans.name: Ryan Graves
ryans.title: Early Uber leader; founder of Saltwater
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Graves** (born 1983) is an American businessman and investor. He was the first employee hired at **Uber**, briefly held the CEO title in the company’s early months, later ran global operations, and now leads the investment firm **Saltwater** [1][2][5].

ryans.name: Ryan Guzman
ryans.title: Actor; Eddie Diaz on 9-1-1
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Anthony Guzman** (born September 21, 1987) is an American actor and former model [17]. He is best known for playing Sean Asa, the male lead in the dance films *Step Up Revolution* (2012) and *Step Up: All In* (2014) [6]. He also played Noah Sandborn opposite Jennifer Lopez in the thriller *The Boy Next Door* (2015) [6][8], and since 2018 he has played firefighter Edmundo "Eddie" Diaz on the first-responder drama *9-1-1* [12][14].
known_for: Sean Asa in Step Up Revolution and Step Up: All In
Noah Sandborn in The Boy Next Door

ryans.name: Ryan Hemsworth
ryans.title: Canadian electronic music producer and DJ
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Hemsworth** (born April 23, 1990) is a Canadian DJ and record producer from Halifax, Nova Scotia [1]. His 2013 debut album *Guilt Trips* won the 2014 Juno Award for Electronic Album of the Year [1]. His album *Numbskull* was released on Topshelf Records on October 21, 2026 [2][4].

ryans.name: Ryan Higa
ryans.title: American YouTuber and comedian
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Higa** (born 1990) is an American comedian and former full-time YouTuber best known for the channel nigahiga [1]. Variety described him as a pioneering influencer who began posting when YouTube launched in 2006 and whose channel held the most subscriptions on YouTube from 2009 to 2011 [1].

ryans.name: Ryan Holiday
ryans.title: Author, The Daily Stoic; founder of Brass Check
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Holiday** (born June 16, 1987) is an American author and marketer [6]. His own biography says he dropped out of college at 19 to apprentice under Robert Greene, author of *The 48 Laws of Power* [1]. He later worked as director of marketing at American Apparel and founded the creative agency Brass Check [1].

ryans.name: Ryan Holmes
ryans.title: Founder and CEO of Hootsuite
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Holmes** is a Canadian entrepreneur best known as the founder of **Hootsuite**, the Vancouver-based social media management platform. As of 2026 he again leads the company as CEO after returning on an interim basis [1][5][6].

ryans.name: Ryan Hoover
ryans.title: Founder of Product Hunt and Weekend Fund
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Hoover** is an American entrepreneur and early-stage investor. He founded **Product Hunt**, a community product-discovery site that became a standard launch venue for startups, and later founded **Weekend Fund**, which he continues to run [1][5][6].

ryans.name: Ryan Humphries
ryans.title: American sales leader and founder
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Humphries** is an American sales leader and entrepreneur based in Austin, Texas [1][2]. Public information about him is sparse and comes mainly from his own LinkedIn profile and posts rather than independent press [1][2][3].
known_for: Curv Group / Floatie Kings sales leadership

ryans.name: Ryan Kaji
ryans.title: American YouTube personality
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Kaji** (born 2011) is an American child entertainer and the on-camera star of the YouTube brand **Ryan’s World** (originally Ryan ToysReview), produced with his family [1][2]. Forbes ranked him the highest-paid YouTube star for three consecutive years (2018–2020) [1][2][3][4].

ryans.name: Matt Ryan
ryans.title: Former NFL quarterback; Falcons President of Football
ryans.lead_summary: **Matthew Thomas Ryan** (born May 17, 1985) is an American football executive and former NFL quarterback [1][2]. Nicknamed "Matty Ice," he spent most of his playing career with the Atlanta Falcons, won Associated Press NFL Most Valuable Player honors in 2016, and in January 2026 was named the Falcons’ President of Football [2][3].

ryans.name: Ryan Miller
ryans.title: Co-designer and brand manager of Disney Lorcana at Ravensburger
ryans.photo_credit: Ryan Miller via Disney Parks Blog / Ravensburger
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Miller** (also legally known as **Ryan Milton** in federal court filings) is an American tabletop and trading card game designer and brand manager at Ravensburger North America, based in the Seattle area [1][3][7][9]. With co-designer Steve Warner, he created *Disney Lorcana*, Ravensburger's first collectible trading card game, which launched in August 2023 in collaboration with The Walt Disney Company [1][2][5].
known_for: Co-designing Disney Lorcana with Steve Warner
Lead design work on Duel Masters and Kaijudo at Wizards of the Coast
Designing The Princess Bride Adventure Book Game (2020)
Co-designing the Warhammer 40,000 Collectible Card Game (2001)

ryans.name: Ryan Moore
ryans.title: CEO of Team Moore LLC; tmgo.to and AdominanceAI
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Moore**, who posts on X as **@0xElGato**, is an entrepreneur based in the United States [1]. His X bio lists him as CEO of Team Moore LLC (@TeamMooreLLC) [1]. He runs **tmgo.to** (short links and QR codes) and **@AdominanceAI** (AI marketing), and builds tech for law firms and agencies [1]. His website is moore.team [1].
known_for: tmgo.to short links and QR codes

ryans.name: Nolan Ryan
ryans.title: Hall of Fame MLB pitcher
ryans.lead_summary: **Lynn Nolan Ryan Jr.** (born January 31, 1947) is an American former Major League Baseball pitcher nicknamed the "Ryan Express" [1][2]. Over a record-tying 27 seasons he pitched for the New York Mets, California Angels, Houston Astros, and Texas Rangers [1][2]. He holds the major-league career records for strikeouts (5,714) and no-hitters (seven) and was elected to the National Baseball Hall of Fame in 1999 [1][2][3][4].

ryans.name: Ryan Perry
ryans.title: Senior Field Engineer at SpaceXAI; co-founder of Pyroscope
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Perry** is a software engineer and founder. He co-founded Pyroscope, an open-source continuous profiling project that Grafana Labs acquired in March 2023 [1][5][7]. He is a Senior Field Engineer at SpaceXAI and has written about running his mobile game Rank'em with a team of Grok Bot agents [1][2][3].
known_for: Co-founding Pyroscope, acquired by Grafana Labs in 2023
Rank'em, a mobile game run by a team of Grok Bot agents

ryans.name: Ryan Petersen
ryans.title: Founder and CEO of Flexport
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Petersen** (born 1980 or 1981) is an American businessman and venture capitalist. He founded and runs **Flexport**, a technology-focused freight forwarder and customs broker based in San Francisco [1][4]. Earlier in his career he worked in his family's import-export business, and in 2007 he co-founded the shipping-data company **ImportGenius** [1]. Since 2023 he has also been a partner at the venture capital firm Founders Fund [3].
known_for: 2021 Port of Long Beach Twitter thread

ryans.name: Ryan Phillippe
ryans.title: Actor
ryans.lead_summary: **Matthew Ryan Phillippe** (born September 10, 1974) is an American actor. He rose from daytime television to late-1990s teen films and later dramatic roles in *Crash* and Clint Eastwood’s *Flags of Our Fathers* [1][5].

ryans.name: Ryan Poles
ryans.title: General Manager of the Chicago Bears
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan C. Poles** (born September 20, 1985) is an American professional football executive and former collegiate offensive lineman who serves as the general manager of the Chicago Bears of the National Football League (NFL) [1][2][9]. Named the seventh general manager in franchise history on January 25, 2022, at age 36, Poles previously spent 13 seasons (2009–2021) in the front office of the Kansas City Chiefs, rising from player personnel assistant to executive director of player personnel [1][2].
known_for: Seventh general manager in Chicago Bears franchise history (2022–present)
2023 No. 1 draft pick trade with Carolina Panthers that yielded DJ Moore and Caleb Williams
Executive Director of Player Personnel for the Kansas City Chiefs (Super Bowl LIV champion)
2025 NFC North division championship with head coach Ben Johnson

ryans.name: Ryan Reynolds
ryans.title: Actor and businessman
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Rodney Reynolds** (born October 23, 1976) is a Canadian-American actor, producer, and entrepreneur. He is best known for starring as the Marvel antihero Deadpool, and for building consumer brands and a Welsh football club alongside film work [1][2][3].

ryans.name: Ryan Seacrest
ryans.title: TV and radio host
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan John Seacrest** (born December 24, 1974) is an American television and radio host and producer. As of 2025–2026 he hosts *American Idol* and *Wheel of Fortune*; he previously co-hosted *Live with Kelly and Ryan* from 2017 until April 2023 [1][2][4][5][6].
known_for: Dick Clark's New Year's Rockin' Eve

ryans.name: Ryan Selkis
ryans.title: Co-founder of Messari; crypto researcher
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Selkis** is an American crypto entrepreneur and researcher best known as co-founder and longtime CEO of **Messari**, a digital-asset data and research platform. He stepped down as CEO in July 2024 after a wave of inflammatory political posts on X [1][2][3].

ryans.name: Ryan Serhant
ryans.title: Founder and CEO of SERHANT.; star of Owning Manhattan
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Matthew Serhant** (born 1984) is an American real estate broker, entrepreneur and television personality [16][2]. He founded and leads **SERHANT.**, a New York–based residential brokerage that also runs media, education and technology divisions [12][16]. He first became widely known as a cast member of Bravo's *Million Dollar Listing New York*, which premiered in 2012 [1][11]. Since June 2024 he has been the central figure of the Netflix reality series *Owning Manhattan*, which follows his company [15][16].

ryans.name: Ryan Shazier
ryans.title: Former Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker; author and Steelers offensive assistant
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Dean Shazier** (born 1991 or 1992) is an American former professional football linebacker, author and coach [11][13]. He played college football at Ohio State and was the Pittsburgh Steelers' first-round pick, 15th overall, in the 2014 NFL draft [3][9]. He was selected to two Pro Bowls [11]. On December 4, 2017, he suffered a spinal cord injury while making a tackle against the Cincinnati Bengals. He had spinal stabilization surgery and never played again [4][5][9].
known_for: Two-time Pro Bowl linebacker for the Pittsburgh Steelers
Recovery from a 2017 spinal cord injury

ryans.name: Ryan Smith
ryans.title: Qualtrics founder; Utah Jazz and Mammoth owner
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Smith** (born June 28, 1978) is an American businessman, the co-founder and executive chairman of experience-management software company **Qualtrics**, and the owner of the NBA’s **Utah Jazz** and NHL’s **Utah Mammoth** through Smith Entertainment Group [1][7][8][9].
known_for: Owning the Utah Jazz and Utah Mammoth

ryans.name: Ryan Tedder
ryans.title: Singer, songwriter, producer
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Benjamin Tedder** (born June 26, 1979) is an American singer, songwriter, and record producer. He is the co-founder and frontman of OneRepublic and a prolific writer-producer for other artists [2][5][6].

ryans.name: Ryan Trahan
ryans.title: American YouTuber and creator
ryans.lead_summary: **Ryan Trahan** (born 1998) is an American YouTuber and entrepreneur known for challenge and travel vlogs, especially his recurring “penny” series [1][2][3]. He left Texas A&M University in 2017 after NCAA rules restricted how he could promote his businesses while competing as a student-athlete, and he pursued YouTube full time [1].
